title: Azure Container Apps - Simply Explained

entities.name: Microsoft Azure
entities.quote: Services like Azure Container instances let you spin up a single container, run a job, and shut it down.

entities.name: Azure App Service
entities.quote: So how does container apps compare to the alternatives? App service has similar pricing for simple apps

entities.name: Visual Studio Code
entities.quote: Developers can deploy directly from Visual Studio or VS code.

quotes.text: Most people don't need either extreme. They want something in the middle, and that middle ground is exactly where Azure Container apps lives.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Positions Azure Container Apps clearly between simple container hosting and full Kubernetes.

quotes.text: Traditional auto-scaling watches CPU or memory. If your CPU hits 80%, spin up another instance. That works, but it's reactive. By the time your CPU is high, your users have already felt the lag.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why event-driven scaling beats classic resource-based autoscaling.

quotes.text: You do not get full Kubernetes flexibility. And that distinction matters. You can't install custom Kubernetes plugins. There's no access to the control plane.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Honestly qualifies the 'Kubernetes without Kubernetes' marketing phrase.

quotes.text: If you're asking yourself should I use Azure Container apps? The answer is probably yes for most new projects. Start there. Move to AKS only if you hit a wall that container apps can't handle.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear default recommendation for choosing a container platform.

chapters.title: Three options: ACI, AKS and Container Apps

takeaways: Azure Container Apps sits between Azure Container Instances and AKS, offering Kubernetes-level features like autoscaling, ingress and revisions while Microsoft manages the cluster.
KEDA, Dapr and Envoy provide event-driven scaling to zero, microservice building blocks and managed ingress with traffic splitting out of the box.
Start new container projects on Container Apps and move to AKS only if you need Helm, custom resources, Windows containers or full cluster control.
hook: Running containers often feels like a choice between a single container and a full Kubernetes cluster that needs its own team. This episode is for developers and small teams who want modern container features without becoming Kubernetes admins: it explains Azure Container Apps, how KEDA, Dapr and Envoy power it, its limits, and what it costs.
